The `|| true` is the point. bd-auto's own `hook` command exits 0 for every
event, so the binary cannot wedge a session by itself — but a config can
still outrun the binary it calls: an upgrade that moves one half, a plugin
directory that moved, a checkout where `make build` has not run yet. Then
the shell reports 127, Claude Code reads any non-zero exit as `block`, and
there is no bd-auto left to fail open on the config's behalf. The wrapper
is the only thing standing there.
Anything that swallows the exit code works; this is the shortest one.
